key_concepts: Bending may change a solid material's size and shape
Pressed solid materials may change size and shape
Pressed solid materials may also change texture
No new material is formed when solids are bent or pressed
Only the physical appearance changes during bending and pressing
Changes in size and shape without a new material are physical changes
Solid materials have definite shape and volume
Properties of solids include size, shape, color, texture, and weight
Examples of bendable solids include plastic rulers, wire, spoons, and paper clips
Examples of pressable solids include clay, ripe banana, bread, and paper cups
Solid materials can also be changed by hammering and cutting
